Retail Workers’ Strike Disrupts Shopping Outlets Across Malaysia

KUALA LUMPUR, 21 June — Thousands of retail employees across Malaysia walked off the job on Thursday morning, leaving many stores shuttered and shopping centres with severely reduced staffing, as workers press for improved pay and working conditions. The unprecedented strike, organised by the National Retail Employees Union (NREU), has affected major outlets, supermarkets, and specialty stores in cities including Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Bahru, and Kota Kinabalu.

At the bustling Bukit Indah Mall in Johor Bahru, roughly 70% of retail stores remained closed throughout Friday. “We have never seen so many shops with their shutters down, not even during festive holidays,” said mall security supervisor Noraini Ismail. “Customers keep coming, but they find most shops are not operating.”

NREU president Abdul Rahman Salleh stated that more than 40,000 workers from over 300 companies have joined the walkout. He said the union is demanding a minimum wage increase to RM2,000 per month, guaranteed annual leave, and better overtime compensation. “Retail workers have faced years of stagnant wages and little job security,” Abdul Rahman told reporters outside the closed headquarters of the city’s largest department store, CityMart. “We are committed to continuing the strike until our voices are heard.”

Some larger retailers, such as MegaSave and ShopNGo, have remained partially open with skeleton crews of management staff. However, shelves in many outlets were sparsely stocked and check-out counters saw long queues. “We are doing our best to serve customers but it’s not enough with so few staff,” said ShopNGo store manager Tan Wei Ming in Penang. “We hope for a quick resolution.”

The Malaysian Retail Industry Association (MRIA) expressed concern about the ongoing disruption. “Many businesses are suffering significant revenue losses,” said MRIA spokesperson Jaya Kumaran. “If the strike continues, it will impact the viability of stores, especially smaller outlets that cannot absorb prolonged closures.”

Analysts say the walkout, now in its second day, is the largest industrial action the sector has seen in over a decade. Talks between union representatives and industry leaders are expected to resume over the weekend. Until then, the majority of retail sites in urban centres remain closed or are operating with drastically reduced capacity.
